entries.title: Find the reusable explanation
entries.text:
Answered the same customer question twice this week?

Save the explanation, remove private details and turn it into one useful public answer.

That is a starting point for OneClickPostFactory: useful material you already have, not a daily demand for new ideas.

entries.title: Give the draft one reader
entries.text:
A draft for founders, agencies and creators at once can lose its point.

Pick one reader and one decision the post should help them make. Keep the other angles for later.

That is the audience choice behind a useful OneClickPostFactory draft.

entries.title: One source need not mean one long post
entries.text:
Your build note explains a decision, a mistake and a workaround. It does not need to become one crowded post.

Separate the lessons; keep each tied to the note.

OneClickPostFactory is designed around reusable angles, not stretching one draft to cover everything.

editorial_reviews.audience: Technical founders answering recurring customer questions
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: The same customer question has arrived twice
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Save and anonymise the explanation before using it publicly
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Recognise usable knowledge outside the content calendar
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: A specific recurring-support scenario rather than the existing source/draft/review or provenance messages
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.

editorial_reviews.audience: Founders repurposing one explanation for mixed audiences
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: One draft attempts to address several audiences at once
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Choose one reader and the decision the draft should help them make
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Understand why audience selection precedes more output
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: Audience focus, distinct from source provenance and approval order
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.

editorial_reviews.audience: Technical founders with detailed engineering notes
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: A single build note contains several independent lessons
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Separate the decision, mistake and workaround into focused angles
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Recognise multiple useful lessons without inventing new product facts
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: Concrete angle decomposition, not cosmetic template rearrangement
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.

entries.title: Agree what finished means before the run
entries.text:
An agent says the feature is finished. You meant it should work for a signed-out visitor; it only checked the signed-in path.

Before the next run, write one acceptance example from the user's perspective. It gives the builder and reviewer the same question to answer.

That is an AI Work Accountability habit behind Proof & State: agree what is being checked before debating whether it passed.

entries.title: Treat skipped checks as their own result
entries.text:
A test could not run because its service was unavailable.

Calling it passed would hide the gap. Calling it failed would blame the feature for a check that never happened.

Record it as not checked, with the reason and the next check needed.

Proof & State's separation of work from verification is useful here: an honest unknown can guide the next decision better than a forced green or red.

entries.title: Check the behaviour requested, not the badge
entries.text:
The task was 'stop duplicate confirmation emails'. The agent returns a green test suite.

Does any test actually submit twice and count the messages?

In a safe test environment, check that behaviour directly and record what was observed. A passing suite only answers the questions it contains.

Proof & State is about connecting a completion claim to the evidence for that claim, not treating a green badge as the whole answer.

editorial_reviews.audience: Founders and engineers delegating product work to coding agents
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: Builder and reviewer have different interpretations of finished
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Write a user-facing acceptance example before delegation
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Recognise an acceptance-criteria mismatch rather than buy a blanket verification promise
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: Pre-work acceptance alignment through a signed-out example, rather than an artefact-identity checklist
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.

editorial_reviews.audience: Engineers reviewing agent work when dependencies are unavailable
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: A missing dependency prevents an intended check from running
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Record not checked separately from passed or failed, with a next check
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Distinguish absence of measurement from a product defect
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: Concrete three-way test disposition extends the earlier permission-scope lesson; it does not claim a new product capability
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.

editorial_reviews.audience: Engineers reviewing a behaviour change made by an agent
editorial_reviews.recognisable_situation: A green test suite does not visibly cover the requested duplicate-email behaviour
editorial_reviews.useful_action: Use a safe test environment to exercise repeated submission and count messages
editorial_reviews.product_connection: Understand verification as checking the requested outcome, not collecting badges
editorial_reviews.novelty_rationale: Replaces the unfiled scope-boundary candidate, which overlaps published PAS-THVAULT-20260911-002; adds a worked assertion-relevance check rather than another scope or hash checklist
editorial_reviews.evidence_boundary: Illustrative reader scenario and practical guidance; no claim of an actual customer incident, measured benefit, current deployment or completed cross-product workflow. Product relationship from the identified reviewed sources.
